Round 1 was already 3/3 direction on my owned set; per the shared directive's Round-2 protocol I change MAGNITUDE and TIMING only, off the incoming boundary STATE, and change ZERO directions. The single instrument round 2 adds that round 1 did not have is the prior session's EXIT CONDITION - last-hour price-direction vs last-hour signed flow (boundary.prior_close_flow_direction_disagreement), close-location-in-range (daytype.friday_exit_close_location_over_flow_shape, generalized to any boundary), and the inherited chain polarity/age/cum_from_anchor (boundary.chain_label_must_track_realized_cum). cross_cutting_mbo_finding: The HE24 exit condition is a TIMING-AND-SIZING instrument in a covering rally, not a direction instrument - and it is the thing that tells you whether a shave is earned or is a self-imposed cap. My three boundaries are three distinct exit classes and each produced a distinct next-session SHAPE. (a) FLAT-PRICE / SELL-FLOW exit (0511 into 0512: last_hour_dir 0, last_hour_sflow -1, close 0.92 off low): the covering bid stopped lifting while sell flow persisted - the close-on-high buys a SMALL overnight extension stub, then the withdrawn bid lets the aligned sell deliver in full. That removes the open-side covering floor I priced into round 1 and is worth +100 of magnitude. (b) ALIGNED-DOWN exit (0512 into 0513: dir -1, flow -1, close 0.16 off low, low at 13:07 = no capitulation flush): the down side is still being delivered at the bell, so the covering resume cannot start at the open - it needs an early-morning base first (realized low 06:47, onset 08:31). This exit class is the one where my shave SURVIVES: the seller who owned the close came back after the spike (ph3 -70). (c) ABSORBED-SELL-UNDER-RISING exit on an UN-DISCHARGED held gap (0518 into 0519: dir +1, flow -1, +580 weekend gap held all day for a +80 intraday stub): the squeeze is live AT the boundary and was never worked off, so the next session's LATE phases are continuation of a stored, un-discharged squeeze - they are NOT the reactive tail I am supposed to hold under, and shaving them is the error. Generalization (+n, not day-specific): in a crowded-short covering regime, size the next session's final phase by whether the prior close DISCHARGED or STORED the covering - a stored squeeze earns its late phase, a discharged one does not.

handoff_out.what_next_day_should_inherit: EXPLICIT WARNING TO D: do NOT read the 0513 ph3 -70 give-back, or the +1000 -> +430 round-trip, as covering exhaustion going into the print. The exit's dir-vs-flow DISAGREEMENT (price up, flow negative) says the crowded short is still being absorbed at the close, which is a directional tell, not exhaustion. Practical consequence for an EIA day: a pre-print flush is a covering ENTRY, not a signal; and an in-line or non-catalytic print REMOVES the excuse the crowded short was waiting for, so the discharge comes THROUGH the print rather than being decided by the surprise sign. Absorption is a REVERSAL, not a damp - if sell is absorbed into the print, the print delivers UP regardless of the surprise sign. Size honestly: the base is the ph3 covering lift plus the ph1 push; a late close-tail on top of that is reactive and not claimable.
